newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan snubs Israeli PM, Arafat to meet president.
newsitem.headline: Jordan snubs Israeli PM, Arafat to meet president.

text.p: Jordan snubbed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday as Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat prepared to meet Israel's president in an attempt to pull Middle East peacemaking out of deep crisis.

Citing differences with peace partner Israel over the sensitive issue of water, Jordan announced that Crown Prince Hassan would not attend a memorial ceremony for seven Israeli girls killed by a Jordanian soldier in March.
Israeli President Ezer Weizman and Arafat were to meet at Erez in the Gaza Strip later in the day in the face of a seven-week-old freeze in Israel-PLO peace talks.

Palestinians have turned to Weizman in the past to press the right-wing Netanyahu to show flexibility. Weizman, an architect of Israel's 1979 peace treaty with Egypt, has no political clout in his mainly ceremonial post but is widely respected.

"I hope that we shall find a way to move the peace process which is stuck in the sand...I cannot say what my hopes are except that I hope something will move," Weizman told reporters at his Jerusalem residence. "I know the man (Arafat), I know some of his colleagues and something will come out of it."
The meeting will be followed by a new mediating mission by U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross, who is due in Israel on Wednesday.

Netanyahu plunged Middle East peace efforts into crisis in March when he gave the green light for bulldozers to break ground for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on land claimed by Israel and the Palestinians.

He had been due to hold talks on Tuesday with Prince Hassan at the Israel-Jordan border site where the girls were killed. Israel's Government Press Office had released an itinerary of what was to have been a showcase Israeli-Arab meeting.
Instead of meeting Netanyahu, Prince Hassan held talks in Amman with Yossi Beilin, a leader of Israel's main opposition Labour party.

"They (Jordanians) are in an awkward situation in the Arab world...(due to the) campaign led by Egypt there is an anti-Israel mood," an Israeli government official, who spoke on condition he not be identified, told Reuters.

"(Jordan) can't have an independent policy simply because it's too weak and too small," he said. "Having not gotten what they wanted by way of the water deal, they decided to pull out of the meeting with Netanyahu."
Israel had promised 150 million cubic metres of water to Jordan under a 1994 peace deal. It has transferred only 50 million cubic metres.

Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon told Israel Radio he had proposed a plan to provide a second allotment of 50 million cubic metres of water six months ago but Jordan had raised new demands which he did not specify.

Commenting on the planned talks with Arafat, Weizman's spokesman Aryeh Shumer told Army Radio the Israeli president would urge him to do more to curb Moslem militants. Shumer declined to discuss other issues Weizman might raise.

Netanyahu demanded a Palestinian Authority crackdown on "terrorism", as a condition for returning to negotiations, after a Palestinian bomber blew up a Tel Aviv cafe on March 21, killing himself and three Israeli women.
Palestinians said they would not back down from a demand that the East Jerusalem settlement and settlement building in the West Bank and Gaza Strip be halted.
"It will make or break the peace process. President Arafat sees no future for the peace process with the continuation of settlements," Arafat spokesman Marwan Kanafani said.
In the West Bank, Israeli police removed dozens of Jewish settlers from a shack near a Jewish settlement and destroyed it along with two other wooden structures which they said were built illegally.

Several settler children were injured by shards of glass and 18 settlers arrested. The National Religious Party said it would not remain in the coalition if Netanyahu continued such actions. The NRP has nine of the 66 seats Netanyahu commands in the 120-member parliament.
